answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with slashable identity bonds plus a one-per-member endorsement graph. To trade, a new agent must lock a deposit and get one non-transferable vouch from an established peer; a fake account therefore costs a fresh bond and a real sponsor who risks being slashed if the clone misbehaves. Attackers also leak structure: their clones all branch from the same funding vertex, so clustering tools flag the burst. Honest agents instead build up a ledge of trust across a wide mesa of activity and vouch independently.
